newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NSW govt says has no SHC timetable.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NSW govt says has no SHC timetable.

text.p: The New South Wales (NSW) state government said on Monday it was still deciding on whether to give Sydney Harbour Casino Ltd (SHC) a tax concession for the high roller market and had no approval timetable.

"As far as the government is concerned the matter is under consideration and we have not set a timetable," a NSW government spokesman told Reuters. "I am unaware of us having reached a conclusion on this," he said
Earlier SHC chief executive officer Neil Gamble told Reuters that he expected the NSW government to make a decision over the proposed high roller tax concession in the 1997 first quarter.
"It is up to them to demonstrate that there are benefits to the taxpayers of New South Wales in any change," the spokesman said.

Sydney Harbour Casino (SHC), which has a 12-year monopoly to operate the only legal casino in Australia's largest city, has battled with the NSW state government for the past 18 months to get a similar tax rate as other Australian casinos.
SHC is seeking a 10 percent tax rate concession for the high roller market from the government, a rate enjoyed by rival casino operators, Crown Ltd, Jupiters Ltd and Burswood Property Trust Ltd.
Gamble has said if the casino operator gets a high roller tax cut it would add about A$10 million to the company's bottom line profit.
